insight.title: Sunlight Is Over 100,000 Years Old
insight.subtitle: The light warming Earth today was generated inside the Sun during the last Ice Age.
insight.notificationHook: Today’s sunlight is from the Ice Age

sections.text: While it takes only eight minutes for sunlight to travel from the surface of the Sun to Earth, those photons were actually created in the star's core over one hundred thousand years ago.

Inside the Sun’s incredibly dense core, newly born light particles cannot travel in a straight line. Instead, they bounce randomly between atoms, taking millennia to slowly fight their way to the surface.
When these photons finally escape into empty space, they instantly leap to the speed of light. The warm glow landing on a leaf today began its journey when mammoths still walked the Earth.
Every beam of sunlight is a relic of the deep past.
